A blue dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) filled with an isometric (triangular) dot lattice: 16 rows of dots, rows alternately offset by half a spacing, 30 dots in the odd rows and 29 in the even rows (counted by pixel analysis), the first row 30. The start of the pattern sits at the top-left, drawn with thin red outlines: 3 regular hexagons filled PURPLE and 10 equilateral triangles filled YELLOW-ORANGE (pale orange). Every hexagon side and every triangle side is 2 dot spacings long. Layout (hexagon H1 left, H2 right, H3 below between them): H1 and H2 sit side by side at the top with one down-pointing triangle above and one up-pointing triangle below their shared vertex (so 2 hexagons and 2 triangles meet there alternately); H3 sits below and between them, its top edge being the base of that lower up-pointing triangle. The 10 yellow triangles, band by band from the top: band 1: 2 up-pointing triangles, one on top of H1 and one on top of H2; band 2: 3 down-pointing triangles (left of H1's top, between H1 and H2, right of H2's top); band 3: 2 up-pointing triangles (below-left of H1, and the one between H1, H2 and H3); band 4: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H1, left of H3); band 5: 1 up-pointing triangle (lower-left of H3); band 6: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H3). Every placed hexagon is therefore surrounded by alternating triangles and hexagons as in P04-pattern-1. Still empty: the down-pointing triangle slot at the right of the H2/H3 junction, and everything to the right of and below the cluster. The rest of the lattice is blank. [Checked against the page picture: confirmed (3 purple hexagons, 10 yellow triangles, hexagon side = triangle side = 2 dot spacings).]

A tessellation inside a thick red rounded rectangle (landscape, no labels), pieces outlined in black: regular HEXAGONS filled light orange (flat top and flat bottom) and equilateral TRIANGLES filled light blue, fitting with no gaps (2 hexagons and 2 triangles meet alternately at every vertex, triangles point up and down alternately in the gaps). The hexagons have horizontal top and bottom edges. By counting: 6 complete hexagons (two rows of 3; the second row is shifted half a hexagon pitch to the left of the first), 20 triangles (5 bands of 4, up-pointing, down-pointing, up, down, up, whole or nearly whole), plus half hexagons and partial triangles cut off by the red frame along the top, bottom, left and right edges (the top strip shows 4 half-hexagons alternating with 4 up-pointing triangles whose apexes touch the top edge; a thin strip at the bottom shows 4 cut-off triangles and slivers of the next hexagon row). At the top-left a small cluster of 3 SQUARES (filled lilac, tilted, not aligned to the grid) and 2 TRIANGLES (filled orange), thin blue outlines, 5 RED dots on vertices. In dot spacings d: each square has side sqrt(5) d (a step of 2 across and 1 down); each triangle is isosceles with base 2d and the other two sides sqrt(5) d, so the triangles are NOT equilateral (base slightly shorter than the other sides; base angles about 63 degrees, apex angle about 53 degrees). items.question_text: A mat has 9 slits. Row 1 is: 1 over, 2 under (repeat). Each next row is the row above moved one slit to the right. Write Row 2 and Row 3 in words, and say after how many rows the rows start to repeat.

diagram.manim_description: Draw a grid of 8 columns by 8 rows of equal square cells, each 100 px, on a 1920 x 1080 canvas with a BG background; the top-left corner of the grid is at (560, 140) and its bottom-right corner at (1360, 940). Every cell has an INK outline of 2 px, except that the vertical line between two cells that touch side by side in one row is left out when both of those cells are over cells, because one strip passes over both and they read as one bar. An over cell (O) is filled MARK_FILL; an under cell (U) is filled BG. Rows from top to bottom, cells from left to right: Row 1: O O U O O U O O (2 over, 1 under, 2 over, 1 under, 2 over). Row 2: U U O U U O U U (2 under, 1 over, 2 under, 1 over, 2 under). Row 3: O O U O O U O O (2 over, 1 under, 2 over, 1 under, 2 over). Row 4: U U O U U O U U (2 under, 1 over, 2 under, 1 over, 2 under). Row 5: O O U O O U O O (2 over, 1 under, 2 over, 1 under, 2 over). Row 6: U U O U U O U U (2 under, 1 over, 2 under, 1 over, 2 under). Row 7: O O U O O U O O (2 over, 1 under, 2 over, 1 under, 2 over). Row 8: U U O U U O U U (2 under, 1 over, 2 under, 1 over, 2 under). Key: two squares of 36 px with INK outline 2 px, the first with top-left corner at (1500, 140) filled MARK_FILL, the second with top-left corner at (1500, 194) filled BG; the word over (INK, text height 36 px, left-aligned at x = 1552, vertically centred on the first square) and the word under (the same, on the second square). Nothing else is drawn: no row numbers, no slit stubs, no paper margin. Keep the grid exactly at this position: the solution figure uses the same grid and adds its labels in the empty margins left and right of it.
